Yearly burden of hospital-acquired infections: cases, deaths and DALYs

Source: R/data.R
hai_burden.Rd

Estimated new cases, deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) per year for five hospital-acquired infections in Germany and Europe, as national totals and per 100,000 population.

Usage

hai_burden

Format

A tibble with 60 rows and 7 variables:

country

"Germany" or "Europe".

infection

One of five infection types.

measure

"Cases" (new infections per year), "Deaths" (deaths caused by the infection) or "DALYs" (healthy years lost).

scale

"Total" (whole population) or "Per 100,000 people" (adjusted for population size, so countries can be compared).

median

Best estimate: the median of 1,000 simulations.

lower

Lower end of the 95% uncertainty interval.

upper

Upper end of the 95% uncertainty interval.

Source

Zacher et al. (2019), Eurosurveillance 24(46), via the BHAI R package: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=BHAI. Prepared in data-raw/hai.R.

Details

A DALY is one year of healthy life lost. It adds years lost to early death and years lived in poor health, so infections can be compared by the harm they cause rather than by how often they occur.

Estimates were produced with BHAI::bhai() (1,000 simulations, seed 2026), which converts a one-day survey into yearly figures. Wide intervals, especially for deaths and DALYs, reflect limited evidence about the outcomes of each infection. Where the Germany and Europe intervals overlap, the difference may not be real.
